paras: The expulsion of Black leaders from Bogalusa, Louisiana, took place in spring 1919, when a committee of white citizens ordered several Black physicians, ministers and property owners to leave town before sunrise. The men left, and the Chicago Defender presented the order as a scheme to take their real estate.

According to the Defender, the men had served on a committee that invited a Los Angeles speaker, printed as "Miss Berrice Anzal," to address Southern injustices. They were also accused of having "burcked" [blocked] alleged labor agents trying to organize Black workers into a union.

White citizens served the men with notices stating that they must "leave town before the sun rises." The first report named Drs. Brazier and L. J. Barkey, Rev. C. H. Hardin, Prof. Lenor, and Messrs. Davis and Brown. Sixteen Black citizens appealed to the mayor, who answered that it was a "district order," not a "city order," and that the men had better obey it. The men, described as taxpayers and property owners, left under cover of darkness, and several families followed after "leave town" signs were posted.

A week later the Defender reported that further appeals had failed, claiming the mayor owed his election to the same white faction. It said efforts were already under way to take their property "by unlawful procedure"; no report of arrests appears.

The only coverage found is two front-page Chicago Defender stories, datelined May 2 and May 9, the second headed "Appeal to Mayor Is Turned Down." The Defender mocked the parish's "strange manner of applying the principles of democracy" and said the men had broken no laws but had angered whites by being progressive and acquiring property. It quoted a white barber dismissing their "sassy actions" in racial terms and later blamed Black "Judas Iscarii" informers.

The two reports name partly different men: Barkey and Brown appear only in the first, while the second adds Dr. James Spivey, Rev. J. Hauptiste and Rev. I. H. Perkins. Its "Rev. Harding" and "Rev. Lennox" appear to match the first's Hardin and Lenor.

bases: A committee of white citizens served notices ordering named Black men to leave town, and the men left under cover of darkness (A1, A2).

accounts.label: Defender correspondent
accounts.gist: A white citizens' committee ordered prominent Black men out of town over an invited speaker and alleged obstruction of labor agents; the real motive was to rob them of their real estate.

accounts.label: Defender follow-up
accounts.gist: Appeals to the mayor failed; the mayor owed his election to the same white crowd; Black informers fed the whites; efforts were under way to take the men's property.

accounts.label: Mayor's reply (as reported by the Defender)
accounts.gist: It was not a 'city order' but a 'district order,' and the men had better obey it.

framing.detail: Opens on the parish's 'strange manner of applying the principles of democracy' to its 'best and most prominent citizens' and calls the whites' purpose 'sinister'; follow-up headline 'Appeal to Mayor Is Turned Down' and denunciation of 'Judas Iscarii' informers.

versions.value: Drs. Brazier and L. J. Barkey, Rev. C. H. Hardin, Prof. Lenor, Messrs. Davis and Brown
Dr. James Spivey, A. Davis, Rev. J. Hauptiste, Dr. A. W. Brazier, Rev. I. H. Perkins, Rev. Harding, Rev. Lennox

conflicts.note: Brazier, Davis, Hardin/Harding and Lenor/Lennox overlap; Barkey and Brown appear only in the first list, Spivey, Hauptiste and Perkins only in the second. The later list is longer and gives churches and posts, but both come from the same paper and the OCR is noisy.
Spelling variants of the same town; the follow-up spelling Bogalusa is used.

sources.note: First report, datelined 'Bosalusa, La. May 2': six named Black men ordered by a white citizens' committee to 'leave town before the sun rises'; mayor calls it a 'district order'; Defender investigator blames designs on their real estate.
quotes: A committee composed of white citizens called upon the above to serve indices which stated they must "leave town before the sun rises."
whose answer was that it was not a "city order," but a "district order," and they had better obey it.
"This parish will not stand for such sassy actions on the part of kitchen-smoked run at," said a white barber in commenting on the affair.

sources.note: Follow-up, 'Appeal to Mayor Is Turned Down', datelined Bogalusa May 9: appeal failed; motive said to be property; Black informers alleged; a different list of seven men driven out; OCR garbled.
quotes: It has developed that several "Judas Iscarii" of our Race are operating in this city, and that the white people are unwisely informed through this channel.
Already efforts have been made to secure the property of these men by unlawful procedure.
